key_insight: Full-field bending strains can identify tension–compression stiffness asymmetry in a bimodulus granular micromechanics model.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports more faithful elastic bending simulations of materials with different tensile and compressive stiffnesses.
method: Measure full-field normal strains using digital image correlation during elastic three-point bending.
Initialize compressive stiffness from manufacturer data and stiffness asymmetry from the measured neutral-axis shift.
Refine stiffness parameters through hybrid optimization matching numerical and experimental strain fields.
evidence_signal: The identified parameters improved agreement with measured through-depth strain profiles and spatial strain distributions over the selected surface region.
watch_item: The largest strain-field discrepancies occur near the concentrated load, warranting caution when evaluating local predictions there.
paper_title: Stiffness coefficients in granular micromechanics determined with three-point bending experiments and digital image correlation for a bimodulus material
